scope: Proposition 3.5 of the manuscript “A uniform Hilbert transform estimate for Lipschitz directions” (preprints/A-uniform-Hilbert-transform-estimate-for-Lipschitz-directions-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 083 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 38d5c48b4d835003), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 39. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every slope t, every collection satisfying (3.1), every line Yt = y0, every horizontal interval I of length l on that line, and every b ≥ 2, the normalized Lb(I) norms of Et, St, and V3   X ℓs=2k ϕs   , V3   X ℓs=2k qT(s)ϕs   are at most CbC(1 + log B)C. The constants are uniform in the line, interval, finite collection, dimension, and number of scales. In particular the assertion holds for every fixed deterministic subcollection with the same constants.
